lead.title: Nous Research ships MISSINGNO, a token-efficient coding and agentic reasoning model
lead.summary: MISSINGNO is a highly token-efficient coding and agentic reasoning model with tool use, free for a limited time on the Nous Portal and usable inside the Hermes Agent framework. The Pokemon-themed drop is the latest step in Nous's push to make open, user-owned agents practical for everyday coding work.

top_stories.title: Sakana AI proposes MASS: verifier-free recursive self-improvement
top_stories.summary: MASS lets a base model propose, execute and grade its own multi-agent workflows, then fine-tunes on the best traces in an evolutionary loop — removing the external-verifier bottleneck. Two cycles on Qwen3.6-27B lifted performance per output token from 1.2x to 1.6x across four open-ended benchmarks.

top_stories.title: Ukrainian drones knock parts of Yandex's largest data center offline
top_stories.summary: Drones hit Yandex's Kaluga facility — Russia's largest at roughly 1.4 million square feet and 63 MW — and state media admitted multiple modules were completely taken out of service. It was the second Yandex data center struck in two days.

top_stories.title: LMSYS shares early SGLang results on NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform
top_stories.summary: The early inference numbers cover attention, MoE and speculative verification for models like Kimi K3 NVFP4, plus end-to-end RL training setups pairing SGLang rollouts with CPU-based agent sandboxes.

items.title: HarnessSQL: training database agents inside realistic execution harnesses
items.summary: Agents trained to inspect schemas, run probe queries and iterate inside isolated executable databases — SFT plus execution-reward RL — took Qwen3-14B from 22.2% to 54.8% on Spider 2.0-SQLite, with transfer to BIRD-Interact and LiveSQLBench.

items.title: Who verifies the verifier? Co-evolving inspectable graders with self-improving agents
items.summary: Makes the grader the evolving object in self-improvement loops: inspectable expressions over small deterministic fault detectors, synthesized from clustered failures and gated against reward hacking.

items.title: OnTrack: real-time monitoring and intervention in LLM agent trajectories
items.summary: Streams structure-aware detection over agent trajectories and intervenes before irreversible actions, instead of paying a safeguard agent's cost per step or issuing post-hoc verdicts after the damage is done.

items.title: SpaceCast-Bench: testing predictive spatial reasoning in vision-language models
items.summary: A 3,862-question benchmark in an observe-transform-infer framework: build a scene from observations, anticipate how an intervention changes it, and infer unseen outcomes — rather than reading off visible relations.

items.title: Embodied Turing Machines: stateful code for robot recursive self-improvement
items.summary: Treats the embodied world as a Turing machine — tape is robot-environment state, rules are policy — with decision-making written entirely in code and tracked from camera images and proprioception.

items.title: Littleguys runs Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw side by side in the macOS menu bar
items.summary: A menu bar app for running multiple coding agents at once; it topped AI-adjacent Show HN launches on October 11.

items.title: Lune is a search engine built for scientific AI agents
items.summary: Launched on Product Hunt, aimed at research agents that need literature and evidence retrieval.

items.title: Galahad offers free open-source long-term memory with a 50M-token window
items.summary: Corbenic AI's memory layer for AI agents is available on GitHub.

items.title: Confident AI releases eval-skills so coding agents can evaluate themselves
items.summary: An open-source toolkit of evaluation skills that let coding agents improve automatically.

items.title: Windows Search turns agentic: results become actions
items.summary: Microsoft's OS search now takes actions on results instead of only finding files.
